THE Buck Converter

Who would've guessed my first board out of the JLCPCB foundry would be a buck converter? The concept itself was deceptively complex. My inexperienced self thought that the matter of converting voltage levels would be trivial, I mean a voltage divider is just 2 resistors. But the buck converter took it to the next level, blessing me with many weeks of debugging and research.

Raspberry Pi Multipurpose Stacker

Lugging around a monitor and keyboard for a raspberry pi gets unwieldy fast, so why not provide a compact user interface. With its lightweight I2C OLED display and the perfect amount of user switches for a good number of programs, who can say no to this plug and play raspi interface?

Keyboard at home

It appears my keyboard didn't make the size cut to fit with the rest of my pc when moving. Should I have maybe packed it in a more appropriately sized box and shipped it separately? Perhaps, but it would be nowhere near as cool. And so this abomination with a slightly modified key layout was born, with one hotkey which automatically turns my pc off with no warning. Pretty volatile, but I'll leave it to scare any curious passerby who should know better than press unfamiliar buttons.

PI_GUI_LITE

Conventionally, raspberry pi users interface with their pi through either ssh or a full setup with a monitor mouse and keyboard. I personally think both these methods are a little unwieldy if you only have your pi on hand, so I started work on pi-gui-lite. In its current state, it can't do much but clone and update certain github repos, but during development, it should gradually give users more and more access to their pi. Check it out at https://github.com/PpMaster37/pi-gui-lite.

The truth and why of the Scrapyard

This website html was not written by own hand, I confess. But if I want some decently nice looking space online to show some stuff I think is cool, then I gotta make do with the tools I got. Webpage and UI design isn’t really my thing, art even less so. Even though I’ve worked with React and all that before to try some interactive pages, the time sink of typing everything out and unintuitive adjusting of block placements around the page is simply not it. Which is why this page is here today. Big ideas from me, hard labor executed by a digital mind. I know to some people it looks painfully obvious and therefore ugly, that really isn’t the point. Just look around at the actual content, trust.
